title: Site comparison preserves the support localization boundary
statement:
Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field and $A$ a finite commutative ring. Let $T$ be a separated finite-type $k$-scheme [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-proper-morphism, def-weil-finite-type-morphism], let $i:C\hookrightarrow T$ be a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion], and let $j:V=T\setminus C\hookrightarrow T$ be its open complement [def-weil-open-immersion]. Let $F$ be an ordinary sheaf of modules over the constant ring sheaf $A_T$ on the small etale site, viewed in degree zero in $D^+(T_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories]. Write $\nu_T:T_{\mathrm{proet}}\to T_{\mathrm{et}}$ for the site comparison morphism [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism] and $F_p=\nu_T^*F$; identify $j^{-1}F_p$ with $\nu_V^*(j^{-1}F)$ by [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-pullback].

Let $c_T^q$ and $c_V^q$ be the degree-$q$ global-section comparison maps induced by the derived adjunction unit [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-global-cohomology]. Let $c_C^q$ be the degree-$q$ map of the canonical support comparison $c^C_{T,F}$ of [lem-pur-support-site-comparison], with supported cohomology defined by the kernel-of-restriction right derived functor [def-pur-support-cohomology]. Let $\partial_{\mathrm{et}}^q$ and $\partial_{\mathrm{pro}}^q$ be the connecting maps of the two support long exact sequences [thm-pur-with-support-exactness], using the same cochain/snake-boundary convention in the two topologies. Then the triples $(c_C^q,c_T^q,c_V^q)$ form a morphism between these long exact sequences. In particular, for every $q\geq0$,
$$
c_C^{q+1}\circ\partial_{\mathrm{et}}^q
=\partial_{\mathrm{pro}}^q\circ c_V^q:
H^q(V_{\mathrm{et}},j^{-1}F)\longrightarrow
H^{q+1}_C(T_{\mathrm{proet}},F_p).
$$
All squares, including the restriction and forgetting-supports squares, commute without an additional sign. These maps and squares are natural in $A_T$-linear morphisms of $F$; in particular all comparison maps and connecting maps are $A$-linear. No constructibility or freeness assumption is imposed on $F$.
